requirement:
After a rejection under {cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`,
a submission whose `rationale` is exactly the UUID that rejection gave MUST
accept the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring the new submission's other
fields. Any other rationale that cites line numbers MUST fail the assessment, so
an assessment rejects at most one submission. The UUID MUST NOT be recorded in
evidence.
rationale:
The obligations in `requirements.authoring.line_numbers.resubmission` are satisfied:

1. **Accept the rejected submission when the new rationale is exactly its UUID.** `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#impl[Rejection]/fn[resubmitted]` compares the rationale to the stored UUID with exact equality and returns a clone of the original arguments. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` checks this before parsing the new arguments and returns the parsed original submission.
2. **Keep the rejected submission unchanged and ignore the new submission’s other fields.** The same path uses only the original argument object, not a merge. `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_rejection_gives_a_uuid_that_keeps_the_rejected_submission]` changes the new determination and asserts equality with the entire original object. It also checks that trailing whitespace prevents the UUID match. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_rationale_citing_line_numbers_is_rejected_once]` exercises acceptance through the conversation harness.
3. **Fail on another rationale citing line numbers, allowing at most one rejection.** `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#impl[Rejection]/fn[decide]` returns `Outcome::Fail` rather than another rejection once rejection state exists. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` turns that outcome into an assessment error. Both referenced tests assert the failure; the conversation test also asserts exactly two requests. They additionally cover a clean replacement rationale being accepted.
4. **Do not record the UUID in evidence.** The UUID override path returns the original submission, leaving the replacement rationale out of the result. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[assess]` builds evidence from that returned rationale. The conversation test asserts the original rationale in evidence and explicitly checks that evidence contains no UUID.

All required tests carry a reference to the subject. No unacknowledged gap was found.

{cite}`requirements.authoring.verifier_prompt`, is otherwise valid but its
rationale cites line numbers under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.detection`, and it is the
assessment's first such submission, the harness MUST reject it instead of
accepting it and continue the conversation. The tool result MUST quote the
matched text, repeat the location guidance of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.judgment_rules`, and give a fresh random UUID,
saying the model may submit once more, either without line numbers or with
`rationale` set to exactly that UUID to keep the rejected submission as it was.
